answer_text:
Here's a comprehensive guide to the **best sources for free 3D game assets** in 2026! 🎮

---

## 🏆 Top Free 3D Game Asset Websites

### 1. 🎯 [Kenney.nl](https://kenney.nl)
This one-person operation has released over **40,000 assets** — all CC0, all free, no sign-up required. The art style is clean, colorful, and remarkably consistent across packs, which means you can mix and match assets without your game looking inconsistent. The site offers 2D assets, 3D models, UI elements, fonts, and audio.
- ✅ **License:** CC0 (Public Domain) — no attribution needed
- ✅ **Best for:** Rapid prototyping, stylized games

---

### 2. 🧱 [Quaternius](https://quaternius.com)
If you're making a 3D game with a stylized low-poly look, Quaternius is essential. This artist has released thousands of models — characters, animals, vehicles, environments, weapons — all under CC0. The signature "Quaternius style" is instantly recognizable: clean geometry, bright colors, charming animations. Assets come rigged and animated, ready to drop into Unity, Unreal, or Godot.
- ✅ **License:** CC0
- ✅ **Best for:** Low-poly 3D games, animated characters

---

### 3. 🌍 [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com)
Poly Haven started as HDRI Haven and has grown into a comprehensive library of 3D models, HDRIs, and textures — all CC0. The models tend toward realistic props and environmental pieces rather than stylized game assets, but they're high quality and instantly usable.
- ✅ **License:** CC0
- ✅ **Best for:** Realistic environments, lighting

---

### 4. 🖼️ [Sketchfab](https://sketchfab.com)
Sketchfab is a huge repository of 3D models, and it has a large collection of downloadable assets. While many are for sale, there's a substantial number of models available for free. The platform's built-in 3D viewer is a great feature, allowing you to inspect every angle of a model before you download it. Just be sure to check the licensing for each model, as they can vary.
- ✅ **License:** Varies (CC0, CC BY, etc.)
- ✅ **Best for:** Wide variety of models, previewing before download

---

### 5. 🕹️ [Itch.io](https://itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-3d)
Itch.io is a popular platform for indie game developers, and it has a massive section for game assets. You can find a wide variety of free 3D game assets, from character models to environmental packs, often with very permissive licenses. The community-driven nature of Itch.io means you'll discover unique and creative assets you won't find anywhere else.
- ✅ **Best for:** Unique/creative assets, complete game kits

---

### 6. 🧲 [Mixamo](https://mixamo.com) *(by Adobe)*
Mixamo offers **2,000+ free animations** with auto-rigging, making it one of the best resources for character animations. Great for humanoid characters in Unity or Unreal Engine.
- ✅ **License:** Free with Adobe account
- ✅ **Best for:** Character animations, auto-rigging

---

### 7. 🏪 [Unity Asset Store (Free Section)](https://assetstore.unity.com)
The Unity Asset Store's free section offers **10,000+ Unity-optimized assets.** It's ideal if you're building in Unity, as assets are already engine-ready.
- ✅ **Best for:** Unity developers

---

### 8. 💎 [Quixel Megascans](https://quixel.com)
Quixel is releasing a final, offline version of Quixel Mixer, along with the option to download **over 800 free Quixel Megascans assets.** It's a pioneer in photogrammetry-based 3D assets delivering photorealistic models, with all assets scanned from real-world objects using purpose-built hardware.
- ✅ **Best for:** AAA-quality photorealistic assets

---

### 9. 🎨 [ArtStation Marketplace](https://www.artstation.com/marketplace)
ArtStation has a popular marketplace full of nearly **60,000 assets**. There are a ton of high-quality free game assets in all kinds of styles. Not just limited to meshes and artwork, the assets also include custom-built textures and elements like clothing and hair.
- ✅ **Best for:** High-quality stylized and realistic assets

---

### 10. 🗃️ [OpenGameArt](https://opengameart.org)
OpenGameArt has been around for over a decade and hosts a massive collection of 2D art, 3D models, music, and sound effects — all under open licenses like CC0, CC-BY, or GPL.
- ✅ **Best for:** Open-source projects, variety

---

### 11. 🆓 [Free3D](https://free3d.com)
A large number of models have a lower polygon count and can be used in games straight away, covering categories like houses, buildings, medieval, fantasy, and more.
- ✅ **Best for:** Diverse categories of game-ready models

---

## 📋 License Quick Reference

| License | Commercial Use | Attribution Required |
|---|---|---|
| **CC0** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| **CC BY** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **CC BY-SA** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes + share-alike |
| **CC BY-NC** | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |

---

## 💡 Pro Tips
- Choose assets from the **same creator or pack** (e.g., all Quaternius or all Kenney), and don't mix photorealistic and low-poly cartoon styles to keep your game visually consistent.
- Always **verify license compatibility** before commercial use, and maintain an asset documentation spreadsheet with source, license, and attribution info.

Happy developing! 🚀
